clinician.trajectory_summary: A 32-year-old Iranian female presented to Rajaei Hospital Cardiac Center with progressive dyspnea at rest. Initial CTPA performed for suspected pulmonary embolism confirmed filling defects in the right main pulmonary artery consistent with PE, incidentally detected a 7mm ground-glass nodule in the left lower lobe, and revealed a 70×75×105mm heterogeneously enhancing left renal mass with extensive tumor thrombosis extending through the left renal vein into the IVC over ~23cm and terminating below the right atrium. She underwent open left radical nephrectomy with concurrent cardiac surgery including IVC thrombectomy and resection of a huge intracardiac tumor from the right atrium under cardiopulmonary bypass. Macroscopic examination showed a 7×6.5×5cm renal mass with sinus extension. Microscopy revealed sheet-like diffuse infiltration of small round neoplastic cells with monomorphic nuclei and fine chromatin. Immunohistochemistry demonstrated positive staining for NKX2.2, CD99, synaptophysin, and chromogranin with negative staining for CK7, CK20, LCA, PAX8, and other carcinoma/lymphoma markers. FISH confirmed EWSR1 gene rearrangement t(11;22), establishing the diagnosis of PNET/Ewing sarcoma. Postoperative course was uneventful; she was discharged after one week and initiated systemic chemotherapy two months postoperatively, continuing on anticoagulation for prothrombotic risk.
